description: The bar chart, titled "Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models," illustrates the accuracy of various models and configurations on a morphosyntactic probing task, with the y-axis labeled "Accuracy" ranging from 70 to 95 in increments of 5. The x-axis displays different model types and configurations, including "1st layer," "random layers," "random layers +B₂," "random layers +L₂," "random layers +R₂," "random layers +permute," "random," "random +B₂," "random +L₂," "random +R₂," "random +permute," and "unperturbed." The bars are color-coded: light blue for "1st layer," light green for "random layers" and its variants, red for the "random" group, and orange for "unperturbed." The chart shows that the "unperturbed" model achieves the highest accuracy, with values of approximately 90.5 for the light orange bar and 91.5 for the dark orange bar. The "1st layer" model shows an accuracy of about 81.5. The "random layers" group, including "+B₂," "+L₂," "+R₂," and "+permute," all have accuracies around 80-82, with the "random layers +permute" configuration having a slightly lower value of approximately 81. The "random" group, including "+B₂," "+L₂," "+R₂," and "+permute," shows a consistent accuracy of approximately 73. The "unperturbed" model has the highest accuracy, while the "random" group has the lowest.
